package `in`.juspay.bbps_sdk_flutter

import io.flutter.plugin.common.MethodCall
import io.flutter.plugin.common.MethodChannel
import org.mockito.Mockito
import kotlin.test.Test

/*
 * This demonstrates a simple unit test of the Kotlin portion of this plugin's implementation.
 *
 * Once you have built the plugin's example app, you can run these tests from the command
 * line by running `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` in the `example/android/` directory, or
 * you can run them directly from IDEs that support JUnit such as Android Studio.
 */

internal class BbpsFlutterPluginTest {
    @Test
    fun onMethodCall_getPlatformVersion_returnsExpectedValue() {
        val plugin = BbpsFlutterPlugin()

        val call = MethodCall("getPlatformVersion", null)
        val mockResult: MethodChannel.Result = Mockito.mock(MethodChannel.Result::class.java)
        plugin.onMethodCall(call, mockResult)

        Mockito.verify(mockResult).success("Android " + android.os.Build.VERSION.RELEASE)
    }
}

repository: https://github.com/juspay/bbps-sdk-flutter
homepage: https://juspay.in/

environment:
  sdk: ^3.9.0

dependencies:

    sdk: flutter

dev_dependencies:

    sdk: flutter
  flutter_lints: ^5.0.0

# following page: https://dart.dev/tools/pub/pubspec

flutter:
  # This section identifies this Flutter project as a plugin project.`
  # The 'pluginClass' specifies the class (in Java, Kotlin, Swift, Objective-C, etc.)
  # which should be registered in the plugin registry. This is required for
  # using method channels.
  # The Android 'package' specifies package in which the registered class is.
  # This is required for using method channels on Android.
  # The 'ffiPlugin' specifies that native code should be built and bundled.
  # This is required for using `dart:ffi`.
  # All these are used by the tooling to maintain consistency when
  # adding or updating assets for this project.
  plugin:
    platforms:
      android:
        package: in.juspay.bbps_sdk_flutter
        pluginClass: BbpsFlutterPlugin
      ios:
        pluginClass: BbpsFlutterPlugin

  #   - images/a_dot_ham.jpeg

  # For details regarding assets in packages, see

  #
  # An image asset can refer to one or more resolution-specific "variants", see

  # in this "flutter" section. Each entry in this list should have a
  # "family" key with the font family name, and a "fonts" key with a
  # list giving the asset and other descriptors for the font. For
  # example:
  # fonts:
  #   - family: Schyler
  #     fonts:
  #       - asset: fonts/Schyler-Regular.ttf

  #   - family: Trajan Pro
  #     fonts:
  #       - asset: fonts/TrajanPro.ttf
  #       - asset: fonts/TrajanPro_Bold.ttf
  #         weight: 700

  # For details regarding fonts in packages, see
